summary: The note traces the rise of esports from 1970s origins to a mainstream industry by 2023. It covers pro players and teams, a young digitally native audience, technology like VR/AR and mobile gaming, economic impacts, education and careers, and international events. It also discusses esports' uncertain Olympic future, noting it was not in the 2024 Paris Olympics.
one_line: Overview of esports' growth from the 1972 Spacewar Olympics to a global industry with pro teams, large audiences, sponsors, education programs, and Olympic aspirations.
key_facts: The first recognized esports event was the 1972 "Intergalactic Spacewar Olympics" at Stanford University, played on the game Spacewar.
Esports began forming its identity in the 1990s with the Internet boom and competitive games like "StarCraft."
Streaming platforms such as Twitch and YouTube Gaming let competitions be broadcast worldwide.
Johnathan 'Fatal1ty' Wendel was one of the first prominent esports figures.
Lee 'Faker' Sang-hyeok is a South Korean 'League of Legends' player considered by many the best in the game's history.
Teams like Team Liquid, Cloud9, and Evil Geniuses became household names, competing in 'Dota 2,' 'Counter-Strike: Global Offensive,' and 'Fortnite' with prize pools in the tens of millions.
As of November 12, 2023, the esports audience largely consists of millennials and Gen Z, who engage via platforms like Reddit and live events.
By December 2023, virtual reality (VR) and augmented reality (AR) were enhancing the viewer experience.
By September 15, 2023, esports had attracted major non-endemic sponsors and profitable media rights deals, and athletes appeared on covers of traditional sports magazines.
Colleges offer esports scholarships, and New York's Excelsior College had competitive teams.
Governments in Asia and Europe have recognized esports as an official sport.
By 2023 many colleges and high schools offered coursework and degrees in game design, esports management, and competitive gaming strategy.
Esports was not included in the 2024 Paris Olympics, though showcases and exhibitions have occurred alongside traditional events.
